title: Communications Officer (Digital & Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji: Complete Guide to the 2026 National UN Volunteer Opportunity in Suva
summary: The United Nations Children s Fund (UNICEF), through the United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme, is inviting qualified professionals to apply for the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment based in Suva, Fiji . This is an excellent opportunity for experienced communications professionals with strong digital media, storytelling, multimedia production, and social media management skills to contribute to improving the lives of children and young people across the Pacific region. The assignment offers professionals an opportunity to work directly with UNICEF s Communication Section, supporting advocacy campaigns, multimedia storytelling, digital communications, donor visibility initiatives, and audience engagement across 14 Pacific Island countries. If you have experience in digital communications, content creation, photography, videography, multimedia editing, analytics, and strategic communication, this assignment provides a meaningful platform to apply your expertise while supporting one of the world s leading humanitarian organizations. About UNICEF UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to protect the rights and wellbeing of every child. Its mission is to ensure that every child survives, thrives, learns, and is protected from violence, discrimination, and exploitation. Within the Pacific region, UNICEF serves: Cook Islands Fiji Kiribati Marshall Islands Federated States of Micronesia Nauru Niue Palau Samoa Solomon Islands Tokelau Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu Together, these countries are home to approximately 2.3 million people , including 1.2 million children and youth , living across more than 660 islands and atolls spread over approximately 17.2 million square kilometres of the Pacific Ocean. Several countries within the region—including Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tuvalu—are classified as Fragile States under World Bank/OECD criteria, making UNICEF s work particularly significant. About the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) Assignment The Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) will be part of UNICEF Pacific s Communications Section and will report directly to the Digital Communication Officer . The Communications Section supports all UNICEF programme areas through strategic communication, advocacy, media engagement, branding, digital outreach, and social media campaigns. The team also leads advocacy around four major regional priorities: Violence against children Climate action Water security Nutrition The selected volunteer will help strengthen UNICEF s digital presence, produce engaging multimedia content, enhance donor visibility, support youth participation, and amplify UNICEF s advocacy messages through innovative storytelling. Assignment Information Item Details Host Organization UNICEF Volunteer Programme United Nations Volunteers (UNV) Position Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) Duty Station Suva, Fiji Assignment Type National UN Volunteer Volunteer Category Specialist Work Arrangement Full-time Work Location On UN Premises Duration 12 Months Extension Possibility Yes Expected Start Date 24 August 2026 Number of Vacancies 1 Main Responsibilities The Communications Officer will undertake a wide range of responsibilities covering digital communications, multimedia production, analytics, storytelling, advocacy, and volunteer engagement. 1. Digital Communication Planning and Publishing The successful candidate will support UNICEF s online communication strategy by: Planning digital communication activities. Producing digital communication materials. Publishing content across UNICEF s website and digital platforms. Supporting social media campaigns. Coordinating promotional campaigns. Developing communication materials aligned with regional and global priorities. Supporting donor visibility planning. Coordinating production timelines. Monitoring donor branding requirements. Maintaining influencer and advocacy databases. Supporting youth engagement initiatives. Assisting online participation campaigns. 2. Multimedia Storytelling A major component of the role involves creating compelling multimedia stories that demonstrate UNICEF s impact. Responsibilities include: Producing social media reels. Editing short videos. Creating photo stories. Designing graphics. Preparing presentation assets. Using existing photo and video libraries. Capturing photographs during events. Recording field missions. Covering programme visits. Documenting humanitarian activities. Working with programme teams to identify impactful stories. Simplifying complex development programmes into engaging public stories. Coordinating interviews. Supporting scripting. Managing filming schedules. Editing content. Incorporating feedback. Preparing final products for publication. 3. Ensuring UNICEF Brand Standards The officer will ensure all communication materials comply with UNICEF standards by following: UNICEF branding guidelines. Ethical storytelling practices. Child safeguarding policies. Image consent procedures. Accessibility standards. Inclusion principles. 4. Digital Analytics and Performance Monitoring The role also requires continuous monitoring of digital performance. Responsibilities include: Tracking engagement rates. Monitoring audience growth. Measuring reach. Assessing impressions. Reviewing click-through rates. Preparing campaign performance reports. Identifying successful content trends. Testing new communication approaches. Monitoring audience feedback. Detecting misinformation. Reporting reputational risks. Supporting positive digital engagement. 5. Supporting the UN Volunteers Programme As part of the assignment, the volunteer will also: Promote volunteerism. Participate in UN Volunteer activities. Celebrate International Volunteer Day. Produce annual volunteer reports. Share field stories for UNV publications. Mentor newly arrived volunteers through the Buddy Programme. Encourage organizations to utilize UN Online Volunteering services. Required Skills and Experience Applicants should possess at least three years of professional experience in communications or related fields. Essential competencies include: Professional digital communications experience. Social media management. Multimedia editing. Photography. Videography. Storytelling. Graphic content production. Copywriting. Editing. Proofreading. Project management. Organizational skills. Communication planning. Digital monitoring. Analytics. Teamwork. Remote collaboration. Strong interpersonal communication. Candidates should also demonstrate commitment to UNICEF s CRITAS values: Care Respect Integrity Trust Accountability Sustainability Desirable Skills Applicants with the following additional skills will have an advantage: Digital analytics experience. Canva. Adobe Premiere Pro. Adobe Photoshop. Adobe Lightroom. Adobe Illustrator. Adobe InDesign. Content Management Systems (CMS). NGO experience. UN experience. Spreadsheet management. Database management. Technical writing. Translating technical documents into public-friendly messages. Educational Requirements Applicants must possess: A Bachelor s degree in: Communications Journalism Or another closely related discipline Language Requirements Applicants must demonstrate: Fluent English (required) Core Competencies UNICEF seeks professionals who demonstrate: Accountability Adaptability Flexibility Building Trust Commitment Motivation Continuous Learning Communication Creativity Ethics Integrity Planning Organizing Professionalism Respect for Diversity Self-management Technological Awareness Teamwork Areas of Expertise Successful candidates should have experience in one or more of the following: Communications Public Information Advocacy Writing Editing Proofreading Research Reporting Knowledge Management Eligibility Criteria Applicants must: Be between 18 and 80 years of age. Be a national of Fiji , a legal resident of Fiji, or hold refugee status in Fiji. Have at least three years of relevant professional experience . Meet the required educational qualifications. Demonstrate fluency in English. Living and Working in Fiji The assignment is based in Suva , the capital city of Fiji. UNICEF notes that: Fiji is considered a middle-income country. Basic services are readily available. The country is widely recognized for its welcoming and friendly communities. Volunteers are expected to arrange their own accommodation and living arrangements. Standard personal security precautions should be observed. Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity UNICEF and the United Nations Volunteers programme strongly encourage diversity and inclusion. Applications are welcomed regardless of: Gender Race Religion Nationality Ethnicity Disability Sexual orientation Gender identity Language Social origin Pregnancy Age Reasonable accommodation is available for volunteers with disabilities throughout recruitment and during the assignment. COVID-19 Requirement Selected volunteers must generally provide proof of full COVID-19 vaccination with a World Health Organization (WHO)-endorsed vaccine before assuming duty, where applicable under UNICEF policies. Certain remote assignments or assignments without community interaction may be exempt according to UNICEF guidelines. Scam Warning Applicants should remember that: The United Nations never charges application fees. No payment is required at any stage of recruitment. Applicants should be cautious of fraudulent recruitment schemes and only apply through official UN platforms. Why You Should Apply This assignment offers communications professionals an exceptional opportunity to: Build experience within UNICEF. Strengthen digital communication and multimedia production skills. Work on high-impact advocacy campaigns. Produce stories that improve children s lives. Gain exposure to international development communication. Collaborate with experienced communication professionals. Support youth engagement across the Pacific. Develop expertise in donor visibility and digital analytics. Contribute directly to UNICEF s mission of protecting children s rights. APPLY HERE Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified in the vacancy information. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as recruitment may close once a suitable number of applications has been received. Visit HERE to learn more about the Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) at UNICEF Fiji. Conclusion The UNICEF Communications Officer (Digital Multimedia) National UN Volunteer assignment presents an outstanding opportunity for experienced communications professionals in Fiji who are passionate about digital storytelling, multimedia production, and advocacy. Working within UNICEF s Pacific Office, the selected volunteer will play a central role in creating compelling digital content that highlights the organization s impact across 14 Pacific Island countries while strengthening public awareness of children s rights and development priorities. Beyond professional growth, this assignment provides the chance to contribute to meaningful humanitarian work, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and support campaigns that influence policy, engage young people, and improve the lives of children throughout the Pacific region. Qualified candidates who meet the eligibility requirements are encouraged to submit their applications promptly through the official United Nations Volunteers recruitment platform. title: Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 in South Africa: Fully Supported Master’s, Doctoral and Postdoctoral Funding for Outstanding Researchers
summary: The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust (OMT) has officially opened applications for its prestigious Postgraduate Scholarships for students planning to begin their studies between January and June 2027 . The Trust continues its long-standing commitment to developing exceptional academic talent by supporting outstanding scholars pursuing Master s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies in South Africa and, in exceptional cases, internationally. The scholarship is designed for individuals with an exceptional academic record who aspire to make significant contributions to academia, scientific research, innovation, development, public policy, and other fields that advance knowledge and benefit society. Every year, the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust awards a limited number of highly competitive scholarships to scholars who demonstrate excellence, leadership potential, and a commitment to using their advanced education to contribute meaningfully to South Africa s future. Applications for students intending to commence studies between January and June 2027 are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026 . About the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust is one of South Africa s leading philanthropic organizations dedicated to supporting higher education, research, youth development, and initiatives that strengthen the country s knowledge economy. Through its postgraduate scholarship programme, the Trust invests in future academics, researchers, innovators, and professionals whose work has the potential to address national and global challenges. The scholarship programme has supported numerous distinguished researchers and scholars whose work has gained international recognition across multiple disciplines. The Trust believes that investing in highly talented individuals contributes directly to strengthening South Africa s research capacity, universities, innovation ecosystem, and long-term development. OMT Postgraduate Scholarship Programme 2027 The scholarship programme supports postgraduate studies at three academic levels: Master s Degree Doctoral (PhD) Degree Postdoctoral Research Each year, only a limited number of scholarships are awarded, making the programme highly competitive. Successful applicants are expected to demonstrate exceptional academic achievement together with clear plans for using their education to contribute to research, teaching, development, or other knowledge-driven sectors. International Study Opportunities The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust also provides funding for international postgraduate study , although this opportunity is reserved only for exceptional candidates. Applicants seeking international scholarships must demonstrate one or more of the following: Their proposed programme is in a unique or highly specialized discipline that is not readily available in South Africa. The intended international institution offers expertise unavailable locally. Study under internationally recognized experts or global leaders will significantly advance their field. International training will contribute meaningfully to their future academic or research career and ultimately benefit South Africa. International scholarships are therefore considered only in exceptional circumstances and require strong academic justification. Fields of Study Applications are welcomed from all academic disciplines , ensuring that scholars from diverse areas of study have an opportunity to compete for funding. However, the Trust specifically excludes: Master of Business Administration (MBA) programmes Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) programmes Programmes with a narrow commercial focus Apart from these exclusions, applicants across sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences, medicine, agriculture, environmental sciences, education, arts, technology, law, and many other disciplines are encouraged to apply. Who Should Apply? The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust seeks applicants who demonstrate exceptional academic ability together with a strong vision for their future contribution to society. Ideal candidates include individuals who: Have consistently demonstrated academic excellence. Intend to pursue careers in: Academia Research Innovation Development Public policy Related knowledge-intensive sectors. Have well-developed postgraduate research plans. Show the potential to become leaders in their disciplines. Intend to use their expertise to strengthen research and development within South Africa. Preference for Local Universities Although international study is supported in exceptional cases, the Trust indicates that preference may be given to students pursuing postgraduate studies at South African universities. This reflects the Trust s commitment to strengthening local higher education institutions while still supporting international opportunities where clearly justified. Scholarship Features Successful scholars benefit from: Funding for Master s studies. Funding for Doctoral (PhD) studies. Funding for Postdoctoral research. Possible international scholarship support for exceptional candidates. Recognition through one of South Africa s most prestigious postgraduate scholarship programmes. Opportunities to advance academic and research careers. Support for research that contributes to South Africa s development. Access to a respected network of scholars and researchers. Selection Process The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust follows a highly competitive selection process. Applications are assessed based on: Academic excellence. Quality of the proposed study or research. Potential contribution to academia and research. Career aspirations. Relevance and impact of the proposed programme. Availability of specialized training where international study is requested. Awards are made entirely at the discretion of the Trust s Trustees. Important Application Guidelines Applicants should carefully observe all application requirements before submitting their applications. Key guidelines include: Applications must be submitted through the official online application portal. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Applications sent by email will not be accepted. Only complete online submissions submitted before the deadline will be reviewed. Scholarship awards are made solely at the discretion of the Trustees. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in disqualification. Application Timeline For studies commencing January to June 2027 Applications Open: 1 June 2026 Application Deadline: 31 August 2026 For studies commencing July to December 2026 Applications Open: 6 January 2026 Application Deadline: 31 March 2026 Applicants targeting the January–June 2027 intake should ensure they submit all required documents before the 31 August 2026 deadline. APPLY HERE Additional Opportunities Offered by the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Beyond postgraduate scholarships, the Trust also offers several prestigious programmes, including: Harry Oppenheimer Fellowship New Frontiers Research Award Sabbatical Study opportunities These initiatives continue to support leading academics and researchers making significant contributions within South Africa and internationally. Why You Should Apply The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarship is among South Africa s most respected postgraduate funding opportunities. Beyond financial support, it recognizes academic excellence and empowers scholars to pursue impactful research that addresses societal challenges. Whether your ambition is to become a university lecturer, researcher, scientist, innovator, or policy expert, this scholarship provides an opportunity to access world-class postgraduate education while contributing to South Africa s academic and research landscape. If you possess an outstanding academic record, a well-defined research vision, and a commitment to advancing knowledge for public benefit, this scholarship represents an excellent opportunity to further your academic journey. Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents early and submit complete applications through the official online portal before the closing date. Visit HERE for more information about the Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 in South Africa. Conclusion The Oppenheimer Memorial Trust Postgraduate Scholarships 2027 offer exceptional funding opportunities for talented scholars pursuing Master s, Doctoral, and Postdoctoral studies. With support available across nearly all academic disciplines and limited international scholarships for outstanding candidates, the programme aims to cultivate the next generation of researchers, academics, and innovators who will contribute to South Africa s long-term development. Since the awards are highly competitive and only complete online applications are considered, interested candidates should begin preparing their applications well in advance and submit them before 31 August 2026 for the January–June 2027 intake. For more global Scholarship opportunities, visit OFY HERE. title: TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 | Up to £25,000 for Higher Education Partnerships
summary: Higher education institutions seeking to strengthen international collaboration can now apply for the TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 under the Going Global Partnerships programme. The second round of funding offers 11 additional grants to support partnerships between institutions in the United Kingdom, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand. The grants aim to promote sustainable transnational education (TNE) partnerships that expand access to quality education, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to positive change in local education systems. About the TNE Exploratory Grants The TNE Exploratory Grants support innovative projects that explore opportunities for transnational education partnerships while promoting inclusive and accessible international education. The programme seeks to encourage institutions to better understand local educational contexts, develop sustainable partnerships, and contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through international education collaboration. Grant Objectives Projects should address one or more of the following objectives: * Promote long-term and sustainable institutional change through Transnational Education (TNE). * Increase access to high-quality and inclusive education. * Improve understanding of local contexts and regulatory environments that support TNE partnerships. * Strengthen operational frameworks for international education collaboration. * Support education initiatives that respond to local needs and priorities. * Contribute to positive changes in education systems and SDG achievement. Funding Details Grant Amount : Up to £25,000 * Project Duration: 17 months * Project Start Date : January 2027 * Number of Projects Funded : 11 * Programme: Going Global Partnerships Participating Countries : Armenia, Bangladesh, Thailand, and the United Kingdom Eligibility Criteria For Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships * The lead institution must be a UK higher education provider with degree-awarding powers. * Partnerships should involve eligible institutions in Armenia or Bangladesh. For Thailand Partnerships * The lead institution must be a Thai higher education institution . * Partnerships should involve eligible UK institutions and meet programme requirements. Applicants should consult the official Call Guidance document for complete eligibility requirements. Benefits of the Grant Selected institutions will receive: * Funding of up to £25,000. * Opportunities to establish or strengthen international partnerships. * Support for exploring sustainable TNE models. * Enhanced institutional capacity for international collaboration. * Opportunities to contribute to educational development and SDG-related outcomes. * Greater understanding of local educational systems and regulatory frameworks. Application Process Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform. Armenia and Bangladesh Partnerships Applicants should use: Going Global Partnerships – Armenia Bangladesh – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead UK institution. Thailand Partnerships Applicants should use: Going Global Partnerships – Thailand – TNE Exploratory Grants 2026 Applications can only be initiated and submitted by the lead Thai institution. Important Dates Clarification Questions Deadline: 23 July 2026 Application Deadline: 2 September 2026, 11:59 a.m. BST Project Start Date: January 2027 Why Apply ? The TNE Exploratory Grants provide an excellent opportunity for universities and higher education institutions to explore innovative international education partnerships. Beyond financial support, the programme helps institutions build long-term collaboration frameworks that improve educational access, quality, and sustainability across multiple countries. Institutions interested in expanding their global engagement strategies and contributing to stronger international education systems should consider applying for this competitive funding opportunity. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the Going Global Partnerships online grant platform before the deadline. Application Deadline : 2 September 2026 Conclusion The TNE Exploratory Grants: Round 2 offer an excellent opportunity for higher education institutions in the UK, Armenia, Bangladesh, and Thailand to build innovative international partnerships that can transform access to quality education. With funding of up to £25,000 per project, successful applicants will have the chance to explore new transnational education models, strengthen institutional collaboration, and contribute to more inclusive and sustainable higher education systems. Beyond financial support, these grants provide a platform for institutions to deepen international engagement, improve understanding of local educational contexts, and develop initiatives that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The programme encourages institutions to create long-term impact by fostering knowledge exchange, enhancing educational opportunities, and supporting positive policy and system-level changes. If your institution is looking to establish or expand meaningful transnational education partnerships, this grant programme could be the catalyst needed to turn innovative ideas into impactful projects. Interested applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements and application guidance before submitting their proposals ahead of the 2 September 2026 deadline. title: Strong Women Grant Programs 2026: Apply for Up to $90,000 in Funding, Mentorship, and Global Network Opportunities

To help remove these obstacles and empower women to achieve even greater impact, applications are opening in August 2026 for a series of women-focused grant programs designed to provide financial support, mentorship, networking opportunities, and access to an inspiring community of changemakers. These funding opportunities recognize women at different stages of their journeys. Whether you are already leading impactful initiatives, developing an innovative project that benefits women and girls, or seeking financial assistance to continue your education or overcome personal hardship, these programs are designed to provide meaningful support. Rather than offering funding alone, the initiative combines financial backing with mentorship, leadership development, peer learning, and access to a valuable professional network, creating opportunities for long-term personal and professional growth. Why These Women s Grant Programs Matter Women continue to face challenges in accessing funding, educational opportunities, leadership positions, and resources necessary to maximize their impact. These grant programs seek to: Remove financial barriers. Recognize exceptional women leaders. Support innovative ideas that benefit women and girls. Invest in future female changemakers. Build stronger communities through women s leadership. Create lasting public impact through funded initiatives. Connect women with mentors and experienced professionals. Foster collaboration through cohort experiences. The programs acknowledge that women contribute to positive change across every profession, industry, and community. Are developing innovative ideas benefiting women and girls. Need financial support to continue education. Face financial barriers preventing future progress. Want to scale their existing impact. title: Autumn 2026 AI Societal Impact Lab Fellowship: Fully Funded Remote Opportunity for Emerging Researchers and Professionals Exploring the Societal Impact of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming nearly every aspect of modern life, from education and healthcare to governance, business, communication, security, and public policy. As AI technologies continue to evolve, there is an increasing need for thoughtful discussions about how these innovations influence society, ethics, democracy, and human well-being. To encourage informed public dialogue and nurture the next generation of thinkers in this important field, the AI Societal Impact Lab has officially launched applications for its inaugural Autumn 2026 Fellowship . This unique remote fellowship is designed to empower emerging voices interested in understanding and addressing the social, political, and ethical implications of artificial intelligence. The fellowship provides participants with an opportunity to collaborate with like-minded individuals, receive expert mentorship, contribute original research, and become part of a growing international community focused on ensuring that AI development benefits society responsibly. If you are a recent graduate, an early-career researcher, or someone passionate about the intersection of technology and society, this fellowship offers an outstanding platform to expand your knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and publish your ideas. About the AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship The Autumn 2026 Fellowship is an intensive online programme created to support individuals who want to critically examine how emerging artificial intelligence technologies are reshaping societies around the world. Rather than focusing exclusively on the technical development of AI systems, the fellowship emphasizes broader societal questions, including governance, ethics, public policy, democracy, social justice, regulation, and the human consequences of technological advancement. Participants will engage in collaborative discussions, workshops, research activities, and mentorship sessions designed to encourage interdisciplinary thinking and meaningful public engagement. The programme aims to build a vibrant network of individuals committed to understanding and addressing the opportunities and challenges associated with rapidly advancing AI technologies. Fellowship Duration The fellowship will: Run remotely for approximately 8–10 weeks Begin in mid to late September 2026 Require approximately 4 hours of participation each week , including: One hour of weekly group discussions or virtual calls Three hours of independent study, research, or project work The AI Societal Impact Lab will provide shortlisted candidates with the detailed programme schedule and specific dates. Fellowship Curriculum Participants can expect a structured programme combining collaborative learning with independent research. The curriculum includes: Weekly virtual fellowship meetings Individual research and analytical work Collaborative group projects Expert-led workshops Interactive seminars Mentorship sessions Preparation of a publishable analytical article The fellowship is intentionally designed to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration among participants with diverse educational and professional backgrounds. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will enjoy numerous academic and professional development opportunities, including: 1. Become Part of an International Community Participants will join a growing network of individuals committed to understanding and responding to the societal impacts of artificial intelligence. 2. Receive Expert Mentorship Each fellow will receive mentorship from experienced fellows at the AI Societal Impact Lab, providing valuable guidance throughout the programme. 3. Collaborate on a Group Project Participants will work together with fellow researchers and professionals on collaborative projects exploring real-world AI-related societal issues. 4. Publish an Original Analytical Article Each fellow will produce an independent analytical piece that will be published on the AI Societal Impact Lab website, providing valuable publication experience and increasing professional visibility. 5. Participate in Workshops and Seminars The fellowship includes specialized workshops and seminars focused on current debates surrounding artificial intelligence and society. 6. Develop Research and Analytical Skills Participants will strengthen their abilities in: Critical thinking Policy analysis Academic writing Public communication Collaborative research Interdisciplinary problem-solving 7. Expand Professional Networks The programme provides opportunities to connect with researchers, academics, policy experts, and fellow participants from diverse backgrounds. Eligibility Criteria The fellowship welcomes applicants from a broad range of academic and professional disciplines. Priority is given to: Recent graduates in the social sciences Recent graduates in the humanities Early-career researchers However, the organizers strongly encourage applications from individuals in: STEM disciplines Arts Other academic backgrounds Other professional sectors Importantly, prior experience or expertise in artificial intelligence is not required . The fellowship values intellectual curiosity, diversity of perspectives, and a genuine interest in examining AI s societal implications. Ideal Applicants The programme is particularly suitable for individuals who are interested in: Artificial intelligence governance AI ethics Technology policy Democracy and digital governance Human rights Social sciences Political science International relations Sociology Philosophy Law Public policy Communication studies Digital transformation Responsible innovation Why You Should Apply Artificial intelligence is becoming one of the defining technologies of the 21st century. Understanding its broader societal implications is increasingly valuable for researchers, policymakers, educators, communicators, and professionals across numerous sectors. This fellowship provides a rare opportunity to: Learn from experienced mentors Build interdisciplinary expertise Develop publishable research Strengthen analytical writing skills Collaborate with peers from different backgrounds Gain exposure to contemporary AI policy debates Build an international professional network Because the programme is conducted entirely online, participants can engage from virtually anywhere while balancing their existing academic or professional commitments. Application Process Interested applicants should complete the official fellowship application form provided by the AI Societal Impact Lab. Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible because spaces are limited and applications are reviewed continuously. APPLY HERE Application Deadline Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until either: 4 September 2026 , or All available fellowship places have been filled, whichever occurs first. Because participation is highly competitive and spaces are strictly limited, early applications are strongly encouraged. Visit HERE for more information about the Autumn 2026 AI Societal Impact Lab Fellowship. Conclusion The AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship represents an exceptional opportunity for emerging researchers, recent graduates, and professionals seeking to explore one of today s most important global issues—the societal impact of artificial intelligence. Through expert mentorship, collaborative projects, dedicated workshops, research publication opportunities, and an international learning community, fellows will gain valuable knowledge and practical experience while contributing meaningful perspectives to ongoing conversations about AI and society. Whether your background is in the humanities, social sciences, STEM, or the arts, this fellowship offers an inclusive environment where diverse ideas are welcomed and interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged. If you are passionate about shaping conversations around responsible AI and technological change, this programme is well worth applying for before the application window closes. title: Bayreuth Humboldt Centre Research Grants 2026–2027 ; Starter and Short Term Funding Opportunities
summary: Introduction The University of Bayreuth Centre of International Excellence “Alexander von Humboldt” (Bayreuth Humboldt Centre) has established itself as a hub for fostering international academic collaboration, advancing interdisciplinary research, and strengthening global scholarly networks. Through its Starter Grant Programme (2027) and Short Term Grant Programme (2026) , the Centre provides researchers from around the world with opportunities to engage in innovative projects, collaborate with local hosts at Bayreuth, and contribute to the university’s vibrant research ecosystem. These grants are not merely financial awards; they are instruments of academic exchange designed to break down barriers between disciplines, cultures, and generations of researchers. The Centre’s mission is to support projects of top academic quality, encourage diversity, and promote gender equality in research. By offering structured funding opportunities, the Bayreuth Humboldt Centre ensures that scholars can pursue ambitious projects while benefiting from the university’s infrastructure, networks, and intellectual environment. The Starter Grant Programme provides €10,000 to support project costs, with an additional monthly family allowance for grantees accompanied by children. Successful completion of a Starter Grant opens the door to a Booster Grant (€20,000), contingent on documented outcomes such as joint publications, workshops, or conferences. The Short Term Grant Programme supports research stays of 1–3 weeks, reimbursing travel and accommodation expenses up to €3,500. title: Skoll Scholarship 2027 at the University of Oxford: Fully Funded Oxford MBA Scholarship for Social Entrepreneurs Driving Systemic Change

title: Middlesex University Visiting Fellows Programme 2026 – Academic Collaboration and Research Opportunities

By joining as a Visiting Fellow, participants gain access to world-class resources, including library facilities, research centres, and interdisciplinary networks. They are encouraged to deliver seminars, workshops, and public lectures, thereby enriching the intellectual life of the university while advancing their own research agendas. The programme is designed to support both academic and practice-based inquiry, offering flexibility for scholars pursuing careers within or outside academia. The Visiting Fellows Programme reflects Middlesex University’s mission to remain at the forefront of academic and professional development. Promote knowledge exchange across disciplines and professional fields. Support interdisciplinary research and practice that addresses global challenges. Strengthen the university’s research ecosystem through active engagement with visiting academics. title: AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship: Fully Remote Fellowship for Emerging Researchers and Graduates Interested in the Social Impact of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming societies, economies, governance, education, employment, and human interaction. As AI technologies continue to reshape the world, there is an increasing need for thoughtful researchers, analysts, and emerging leaders who can examine their societal implications from ethical, political, legal, cultural, and social perspectives. To support this growing need, the AI Societal Impact Lab has launched its inaugural Autumn 2026 Fellowship , a fully remote fellowship program designed to cultivate the next generation of thinkers exploring the socio-political impact of emerging AI technologies. The fellowship offers a unique opportunity for recent graduates, early-career researchers, and professionals from diverse academic backgrounds to participate in an engaging learning experience that combines mentorship, collaborative projects, workshops, and original research publication. Running for approximately 8–10 weeks beginning in mid-to-late September 2026 , the program provides participants with the opportunity to deepen their understanding of AI s societal implications while contributing meaningful ideas to public discussions surrounding one of the most important technological developments of our time. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the fellowship is full or 4 September 2026 , whichever comes first. Since spaces are limited, interested applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible. About the AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship The Autumn 2026 Fellowship is the inaugural fellowship program established by the AI Societal Impact Lab to encourage informed public dialogue about the opportunities and challenges presented by artificial intelligence. Rather than focusing on technical AI development, the fellowship emphasizes understanding AI through social, political, ethical, cultural, and interdisciplinary lenses. The program seeks to amplify emerging voices capable of contributing fresh perspectives on how AI influences societies, institutions, governance, and everyday life. Participants will collaborate with fellow researchers while receiving mentorship from experts affiliated with the AI Societal Impact Lab. Fellowship Objectives The fellowship aims to: Foster informed public discussions about artificial intelligence. Support emerging researchers interested in AI governance and societal impact. Build a diverse international community of future AI policy thinkers. Encourage interdisciplinary collaboration. Produce thoughtful analytical work that contributes to ongoing conversations about AI and society. Equip participants with research and communication skills relevant to emerging technology. Fellowship Duration The Autumn 2026 Fellowship will: Run remotely. Last approximately 8–10 weeks . Begin in mid-to-late September 2026 . Operate entirely online. Specific program dates and the detailed curriculum will be shared with shortlisted candidates. Weekly Time Commitment The fellowship has been designed to be flexible for participants who may be working or studying. Participants should expect to dedicate approximately four hours per week , including: One hour participating in a weekly fellowship call. Three hours completing independent reading, research, writing, or collaborative work. This manageable schedule enables fellows from different parts of the world to participate without requiring full-time commitment. Fellowship Curriculum The curriculum focuses on examining artificial intelligence through interdisciplinary perspectives. Although detailed weekly topics will be provided later, participants can expect activities that include: Guided discussions on AI and society. Collaborative group learning. Critical analysis of AI-related issues. Independent research. Writing analytical essays. Interactive workshops. Expert seminars. Group project development. Mentorship sessions. The fellowship emphasizes intellectual curiosity, thoughtful discussion, and collaborative problem-solving rather than technical AI programming. Who Can Apply? The fellowship welcomes applicants from diverse educational and professional backgrounds. Primary target applicants include: Recent graduates in Social Sciences. Recent graduates in Humanities. Early-career researchers. However, the AI Societal Impact Lab explicitly encourages applications from individuals with different academic disciplines, including: STEM fields. Arts. Design. Interdisciplinary programs. Other academic backgrounds. The organizers value diversity of perspectives and representation as much as prior subject expertise. Is Previous AI Experience Required? No. Applicants are not required to have previous experience researching artificial intelligence. While prior knowledge or experience related to AI is considered beneficial, it is not a prerequisite for selection. Applicants with strong analytical thinking, curiosity, and interest in AI s societal implications are encouraged to apply. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will receive numerous professional and academic benefits throughout the program. These include: 1. Expert Mentorship Participants will receive mentorship from one of the fellows at the AI Societal Impact Lab, gaining valuable guidance throughout the fellowship. 2. Collaborative Group Project Fellows will work together on a collaborative project addressing important questions surrounding artificial intelligence and society. This provides opportunities to: Build teamwork skills. Learn from peers. Develop interdisciplinary approaches. Expand professional networks. 3. Publish Your Own Analytical Article Each fellow will produce an original analytical piece that will be published on the AI Societal Impact Lab website. Publishing an article provides participants with: Academic visibility. Writing experience. A professional publication for their portfolio. Increased credibility in AI policy and societal research. 4. Workshops and Seminars Participants will attend dedicated workshops and seminars covering emerging issues related to AI and society. These sessions help fellows: Strengthen analytical skills. Learn from experienced researchers. Explore interdisciplinary perspectives. Develop practical policy insights. 5. Join an International Community The fellowship seeks to build a community of individuals committed to understanding and addressing the societal consequences of rapid technological advancement. Participants will become part of a growing international network of researchers, graduates, and professionals interested in AI governance and social impact. Click HERE to learn more. Why You Should Apply The AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn Fellowship offers several compelling advantages. Participants will have the opportunity to: Build expertise in one of today s fastest-growing interdisciplinary fields. Learn directly from experienced mentors. Publish original analytical work. Collaborate with talented peers. Develop research and policy analysis skills. Expand their professional network. Gain experience examining real-world AI challenges. Enhance their CV with a recognized international fellowship. For individuals interested in technology policy, ethics, governance, sociology, political science, law, philosophy, public policy, or interdisciplinary AI research, this fellowship provides an excellent platform for professional growth. How to Apply Applicants should submit their application by completing the official online application form provided by the AI Societal Impact Lab. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible due to the limited number of fellowship spaces. The detailed fellowship schedule and curriculum will be shared with shortlisted applicants during the selection process. Application Timeline Applications are currently open. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis , meaning submissions are evaluated as they are received. The application process will close when either: All fellowship places have been filled, or The final application deadline is reached. Because selection occurs on a rolling basis, submitting an early application significantly improves the likelihood of consideration. Application Deadline Applications close on 4 September 2026, or earlier if all fellowship places are filled. Applicants are strongly encouraged not to wait until the final deadline, as spaces are strictly limited. APPLY HERE Why This Fellowship Matters Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing public policy, labor markets, education, healthcare, democracy, media, and international relations. Understanding these transformations requires more than technical expertise—it requires thoughtful interdisciplinary perspectives that consider ethics, governance, culture, inequality, and public interest. The AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship seeks to develop exactly these kinds of emerging voices by providing participants with mentorship, collaboration opportunities, publication experience, and access to an international network of individuals committed to responsible AI discourse. Whether you are a recent graduate in sociology, philosophy, political science, computer science, or another field, this fellowship provides an outstanding opportunity to contribute to meaningful conversations shaping the future of AI and society. Conclusion The AI Societal Impact Lab Autumn 2026 Fellowship is an excellent opportunity for recent graduates and early-career researchers who want to explore the broader societal implications of artificial intelligence. With a flexible remote format, a manageable weekly commitment of approximately four hours, and a strong emphasis on diversity of thought and representation, the fellowship is accessible to applicants from a wide range of academic backgrounds.
